title: Philippines requests 6 Chinook helicopters under $2-B US financing
summary: The Philippine government, through the Department of National Defense (DND), has requested the purchase of six CH-47 Chinook helicopters under the $2-billion US Foreign Military Financing, Defense…

blocks.text: The Philippines, through the Department of National Defense (DND), has requested the purchase of six CH-47 Chinook helicopters under the $2-billion US Foreign Military Financing, Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro said on Thursday.

“Nag-request kami sa US government doon sa $2-billion financing ng anim na Chinook. That is the only thing I can disclose out of that package,” Teodoro said after the closing ceremony of the Armed Forces of the Philippines’ Joint Exercise Dagat-Langit-Lupa.
(We made a request to the US government regarding the $2-billion financing for six Chinooks. That is the only thing I can disclose out of that package.)
He said that all six brand-new helicopters could be delivered as early as 2029 if the US agrees to prioritize the Philippine order; otherwise, delivery could take up to six years.
Aside from the acquisition, the request also covers integrated logistics support and crew training.
Teodoro said a Chinook helicopter could carry about four times the load of a Black Hawk, pointing out the time and logistical space it would save.

“A Chinook can carry about 4 times a Black Hawk, so it saves you time, and it saves you logistical space. Kasi hindi minamano-mano ‘yan. Nilo-load na lang ng ano yan, ng lifter, loader,” the Defense chief said.
(A Chinook can carry about four times a Black Hawk, so it saves you time, and it saves you logistical space. Because you don't load that manually—it's loaded using a lifter or loader.)

“So, time is more than a quarter of one-fourth the time na kailangan mong i-load yung Black Hawk. 'Yun lang ang kailangan mo sa Chinook. Kaya mong magbuhat ng malalaking kanyon. Kaya mo magbuhat ng sasakyan na may pasahero pa,” he added.

(So, loading takes less than a quarter of the time you need to load a Black Hawk. That’s all you need for a Chinook. You can carry large artillery pieces, and you can even carry a vehicle with passengers still inside.)
However, Teodoro raised concerns about the helicopters’ maintenance costs, which he sees as a bigger challenge than building basing infrastructure for the aircraft.
“Basing ng anim na Chinook, e kayang-kaya. Maintenance, maintenance problema dun,” he said.
(Basing six Chinooks—we can easily manage that. Maintdenance is the problem there.)

Last week, the White House announced that Manila and Washington had agreed to work toward a foreign military financing loan exceeding $2 billion to supply the Philippines with defense and security capabilities from US suppliers. –Lyjah Tiffany Bonzo/NB, GMA News
